title: Chilli con Carne
subtitle: Slow-cooked beef, kidney bean, and chilli stew
excerpt: Minced beef and kidney beans cooked low and slow in a deeply spiced tomato sauce with ancho, cumin, and smoked paprika. Better the next day, better still the day after that.

recipe.sourceNotes: Chili con carne (literally 'peppers with meat') originated in the American Southwest and Texas, where it is considered the official state dish of Texas, and has been absorbed into British cooking as a staple of the home kitchen. Debate around the authentic version is longstanding: Texan purists insist it should contain no beans, while the British-American version almost always does. The dish benefits from a long, slow cook and improves significantly on reheating, as the fat redistributes and the flavour deepens.

recipeTools.notes: Heavy-based pan to prevent scorching during the long simmer.

content.text: Brown the mince in batches without crowding the pan. If you tip all the meat in at once it will steam rather than brown, and the chilli will lack the deep base flavour you are after. Cook the onion and spices properly before adding the liquid: at least 10 minutes for the onion and 2 minutes for the spices. The beans go in towards the end so they hold their shape.

Heat the oil in a large pan over high heat. Brown the mince in 2 batches for 4 to 5 minutes per batch. Remove each batch and set aside. Drain off excess fat if needed, leaving about 2 tablespoons in the pan.

Reduce the heat to medium. Cook the onion and red pepper for 10 minutes until soft. Add the garlic, cumin, coriander, smoked paprika, chilli powder, and chilli flakes. Stir for 2 minutes. Add the tomato puree and stir for 1 minute.
Return the mince to the pan. Add the tinned tomatoes and stock. Season. Stir well. Bring to a simmer, then reduce the heat to very low, cover partially, and cook for 1 hour, stirring occasionally.

Add the kidney beans and chocolate. Stir through and cook for a further 15 minutes. Taste and adjust seasoning. Serve with rice, jacket potato, or tortilla chips, with soured cream and grated Cheddar alongside.
